correctness.rationale: On the zero-sum space the cyclic H=-L is strictly positive; the Jacobian K diag(c)L has real transverse inertia determined by the quadratic form sum_i c_i x_i². Two nonpositive coefficients yield a nonpositive vector e_i−e_j. Exactly one zero and all other positive is positive definite; exactly one negative and all other positive gives the exact reciprocal-cosine threshold by weighted Cauchy–Schwarz, with simple neutral equality and one unstable direction beyond. The curvature vector q=(nt,-t,...,-t), n=N−1, lies in the image of L and is realized by an actual phase vector; force balance gives Δ=K[sin(nt)+sin t]. Strict concavity on 0<t<π/n gives unique nondegenerate fold t*, stable/unstable sides and two roots only within this family; Taylor expansion gives K/(2n²)+O(Kn^-3) mixed-curvature window. Independent eigenvalue calculation checked 1170 random/zero sign patterns N=3..15 and independently bracketed 13 scalar folds.

value.rationale: The physically natural single-frequency impurity demonstrates stable synchronization with one negative local cosine, locates the saddle-node and quantifies the collapsing finite-size forcing window at order K/N². It resolves a substantive branch question left by principal-arcsine analysis, not an arbitrary parameter shift. Global locking among all curvature and winding sectors is excluded.

limitations: Local orbital exponential stability and one real-curvature impurity family only; no global stability and no proof of all locking branches.
